statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-49835 (GHSA-9c54-x2g4-v92j, GO-2026-5851): the Sigstore Timestamp Authority server's wrapMetrics HTTP middleware recorded the raw request path and method as Prometheus metric labels, so an unauthenticated client sending requests with random paths or methods could make the server's memory grow without bound. It affects github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/v2 up to and including 2.0.6 and is fixed in 2.1.0 by commit 506ec57b (https://github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/commit/506ec57b6ac2ea1e4739322e47453469425b69b5), which changes only pkg/generated/restapi/configure_timestamp_server.go and its test. Sources: https://github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/security/advisories/GHSA-9c54-x2g4-v92j and https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5851. We checked every scout-sbom-indexer-dev package published for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository as of 27 November 2026: 25 builds, 1.20.4-r1 to the current 1.30.0-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64 (50 packages). Each package holds one file, /sbom-indexer, a statically linked Go program for Linux built with CGO_ENABLED=0 (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). We read the program in full from every package, except 1.26.0-r3, whose program has the same SHA-1 checksum, recorded in its package header, as the 1.26.0-r2 program we read. The -dev program is built without the -w linker flag and without -trimpath; its Go release and module versions are the same as those of the scout-sbom-indexer program of the same build. Its Go build information lists github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/v2, with no replacement and the same on both architectures: v2.0.6 in 1.20.4-r1 to 1.21.0-r3, v2.1.0 in 1.23.1-r0, v2.1.2 in 1.23.1-r1 to 1.30.0-r0. Reading the program's Go function table in every build (runtime.main found in every build as a control) shows that the only timestamp-authority function linked is the initializer of the client-side package pkg/verification (verification.init); no function from the server's pkg/generated/restapi package, including wrapMetrics, is in the function table of any build. A byte search of every build, which also finds the names of functions the compiler inlined, finds none of wrapMetrics or pkg/generated/restapi; the only timestamp-authority/v2/pkg/ names are verification..inittask and verification.init, while the same search finds runtime.main in every build. So the timestamp-authority server code this advisory concerns is not present in any build, whichever timestamp-authority version the build information names. Debian 13 marks its golang-github-sigstore-timestamp-authority package no-dsa for this CVE (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-49835); this decision rests on the code in these builds, not on that status.

CVE-2026-49835 (GO-2026-5851, GHSA-9c54-x2g4-v92j): the Sigstore Timestamp Authority server's wrapMetrics HTTP middleware records the raw request path and method as Prometheus metric labels, so an unauthenticated client sending requests with random paths or methods makes the server's memory grow without bound. It is fixed in github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/v2 2.1.0. The Go vulnerability database lists no symbols; the fix commit changes only wrapMetrics in pkg/generated/restapi/configure_timestamp_server.go, the server's REST API setup. Sources: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5851, https://github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/security/advisories/GHSA-9c54-x2g4-v92j, https://github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/commit/506ec57b6ac2ea1e4739322e47453469425b69b5 . We checked every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the repository index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a statically linked Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0. We read its Go build information (go version -m) and its function table (go tool nm), and searched its raw bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions. The Go build information lists github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/v2 2.0.3 in builds up to 0.69.3-r5 and 2.0.6 from 0.69.3-r6 to 0.71.2-r0, inside the affected range, then 2.1.0 and 2.1.2 in 0.71.2-r1 to 0.71.2-r3; builds from 0.73.0-r0 on do not contain the module. In every build that contains it, the only timestamp-authority function in the function table is the package initializer github.com/sigstore/timestamp-authority/v2/pkg/verification.init, from the client-side verification package. No function of the server packages pkg/generated/restapi or pkg/server is present, including wrapMetrics and setupGlobalMiddleware, while runtime.main is. The raw-byte search of every build finds timestamp-authority names only from pkg/verification (its initializer and the source path of verify_request.go), and no pkg/generated/restapi, pkg/server or wrapMetrics name. As a positive control, the same function-table and byte searches on a program built against timestamp-authority 2.0.6 that builds the server and calls ConfigureAPI find restapi.wrapMetrics.func1, setupGlobalMiddleware and configureAPI, and wrapMetrics itself when built without inlining. The control programs were built with Go 1.27.1, CGO_ENABLED=0, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. trivy does not contain the timestamp server code, so the vulnerable code is not in the shipped binary.
